_comment: The build envelope every Gradle root in the suite has to stay inside.
Dependabot cannot see compileSdk, minSdk or the Compose compiler wiring - it
only sees version numbers. Left alone it proposes AndroidX releases whose AAR
metadata demands a newer platform than the suite compiles against, and the
PR fails in CI with a CheckAarMetadata error nobody has to read twice.
Each ceiling below is the highest version that is PROVEN GREEN on the current
envelope, plus the evidence for why the next step is blocked. Raising a
ceiling is a deliberate act: change the envelope first (compileSdk / AGP /
Kotlin / Compose plugin), see CI go green, then lift the ceiling.
tools/check_gradle_envelope.py enforces this file in both directions:
- no root declares a version above its ceiling
- .github/dependabot.yml ignores minor+major for every ceiling coordinate
in every directory that declares it
so the ignore rules cannot be silently dropped again (they were, in
9f5d266d, which is what produced PRs #122 #125 #126 #132).
The Android Gradle toolchain is intentionally root-specific.
The repo root, ticker/android, shift, motion-plugin, and doctor remain at
AGP 8.5.2 / external Kotlin 1.9.24. AGP 8.13.2 fails on Gradle 9.7.0
because it binds an internal Gradle API removed in 9.6.0 (PRs #144-#149).
Core EQ is an isolated Gradle root and has migrated to AGP 9.4.0, Gradle
9.7.0, AGP built-in Kotlin, and compile/target API 37. AGP 9.4 requires
Gradle 9.6.0 and supports API 37; do not apply the Core EQ exception to
the other roots without a separate migration and CI evidence.
From Kotlin 2.0 the Compose compiler ships as its own Gradle plugin and
composeOptions.kotlinCompilerExtensionVersion must be deleted. doctor/
pins that DSL to 1.5.14, which the Compose compiler ties to Kotlin
1.9.24 exactly - so any Kotlin 2.x bump breaks doctor/ before it ever
reaches a compileSdk check. The gate asserts this so the requirement
outlives the memory of it.

ceilings.reason: The repo root and the Core Line, Shift, Motion, and Doctor roots remain on AGP 8.5.2. AGP 8.13.2 fails on their Gradle 9.7.0 wrapper because it binds org.gradle.api.problems.internal.InternalProblems, removed in Gradle 9.6.0. Core EQ is an explicitly tested per-root exception at AGP 9.4.0.

reasonByDirectory./coreeq: Core EQ has its own Gradle root and has migrated to AGP 9.4.0 with built-in Kotlin, Gradle 9.7.0, and compileSdk/targetSdk 37. AGP 9.4 supports API 37 and requires Gradle 9.6.0 or newer.

ceilings.reason: 5.5.0 pulls com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp-android:5.5.0, whose AAR metadata needs compileSdk 37; doctor/ compiles at 35 on AGP 8.5.2, so :app:checkDebugAarMetadata fails (PR #159). Which 5.x release first crosses a compileSdk the suite can reach is not proven, so the cap sits at 4.12.0, the last green release, and lifts with the compileSdk steps in the migration list.
1.15.0 needs compileSdk 35; 1.17.0 needs compileSdk 36 and AGP 8.9.1; 1.19.0 needs compileSdk 37 and AGP 9.1.0. Five of six modules compile at 34.
1.8.0 needs compileSdk 36 and raises its own minSdk to 23. The icon pack declares minSdk 21 for Android 5.x Fire TV hardware, so 1.8.0 fails the manifest merge before it fails AAR metadata.
1.4.0 will only compile against API 35 or higher; the modules that declare it compile at 34.
1.5.0 needs compileSdk 35 and 1.10.0 needs compileSdk 36; shift/ compiles at 34. 1.9.0 also raises minSdk to 23, which shift/ at 26 survives but the rest of the suite would not.
Released in lockstep with media3-exoplayer; same compileSdk floors.
Released in lockstep with media3-exoplayer; same compileSdk floors.

Current BOMs pull Compose libraries that need compileSdk 36-37, and 2026.09.00 in particular needs 37. doctor/ compiles at 35. The BOM also cannot move before Kotlin 2.x lands, because it drags the Compose compiler plugin requirement with it.

It has to move with androidx.compose:compose-bom, not ahead of it. Taking activity-compose 1.10.x alone drags a newer Compose runtime onto the classpath than the 2024.06.00 BOM pins, which fails as a NoSuchMethodError at runtime or in unit tests rather than as a build error - the worst shape of failure to diagnose. doctor/ compiles at 35, so compileSdk is not the binding constraint here; the BOM is.

1.7.0 needs the serialization compiler plugin at 2.0.0-RC1 or newer and is explicitly rejected by older plugins; doctor/ pins that plugin at 1.9.24. 1.6.x is the line built for Kotlin 1.9.x. 1.11.0 additionally requires kotlin-stdlib 2.3.20. This ceiling lifts the moment Kotlin 2.x lands.

Releases from 1.9.0 on are compiled with Kotlin 2.x, whose binary metadata a Kotlin 1.9.24 compiler cannot read - it fails with 'Module was compiled with an incompatible version of Kotlin'. Which exact release crosses the line is not documented per version, so the cap sits at the last proven-green one and moves with the Kotlin migration rather than by guesswork.

Kotlin 2.0 moves the Compose compiler out of the Kotlin repository into org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose. doctor/ still sets composeOptions.kotlinCompilerExtensionVersion = "1.5.14", which is hard-tied to Kotlin 1.9.24. All five Kotlin modules also use the kotlinOptions DSL rather than compilerOptions (glyphs/ is Java-only). This is a source migration, not a version bump.
Must match org.jetbrains.kotlin.android exactly, so it is blocked for the same reason and moves with it.

_comment: The remaining ceilings still describe the five older suite roots. Core EQ
has a separate Gradle root and its API 37 / AGP 9.4 migration is recorded
as the one explicit per-root exception above. Keep changes scoped until CI
proves a separate toolchain migration for another root.
steps: Decide whether the repo-root icon pack still needs Android 5.x Fire TV support at minSdk 21. That question is separate from Core EQ, which now starts at Android 11 / API 30.
Keep the repo root, ticker/android, shift, motion-plugin, and doctor on the proven AGP 8.5.2 / Kotlin 1.9.24 envelope until each has a separately tested migration.
Core EQ is the isolated exception: AGP 9.4.0, Gradle 9.7.0, AGP built-in Kotlin, compileSdk/targetSdk 37; its Dependabot ceiling and workflow platform are checked independently.
For the remaining roots, resolve the AGP/wrapper pair before moving AGP, then migrate doctor/ off the Kotlin 1.9 Compose compiler DSL before raising Kotlin on the roots that still use it.
Raise compileSdk per root only after its AGP supports that API level and its CI workflow installs the matching platform; then lift the matching AndroidX ceilings as each root goes green.
Only then unblock androidx.core, appcompat, recyclerview, media3, compose-bom, okhttp, and external Kotlin plugins in the directories that actually declare them.
